title: The bathroom
description: Name the things in a bathroom and say what you use them for.
grammar: gender and articles, and the words for things you use
grammarNote: Most of these nouns are masculine, which is the opposite of the bedroom.

explanation.summary: The bathroom has its own small set of nouns. Most of them end in -o and are masculine, and several of them are used with a piece of clothing or a room rather than on their own.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El lavabo, el inodoro and el secador are all masculine. La ducha and la bañera are feminine. One of them is a phrase with its own article inside it: la pasta de dientes is a feminine noun with de dientes attached, and you say una pasta de dientes, never un pasta.

sections.heading: Saying what you use
sections.body: You already know tener, so you can say what a person has and what they need. Para says what something is for: el peine es para el pelo, the comb is for the hair. In a shop you ask for it with un or una, and the noun tells you which one.

examples.es: el peine es para el pelo
examples.en: the comb is for the hair

examples.es: el secador es para el pelo
examples.en: the hairdryer is for the hair

items.note: Masculine: el champú. The accent marks the stress.
Feminine: la pasta de dientes. You say una pasta de dientes.

drills.meaning: the sink is in the bathroom
I need a comb for the hair
